rv.q: But every so often, the score and the staging melt into a quieter, creepier form of enchantment that summons some of the shimmering mystery of Welty's book.
Director Alex Timbers has turned genres gleefully on their edges with "Andrew Jackson" and "Here Lies Love.

Timbers draws from his usual bag of magic tricks, prop jokes, unexpected taxidermy, and winking meta-theatricality to keep the eye and attention engaged at all times. Even so, the story, having been pulled away from any real engagement with its dark fundamentals, now seems like an excuse instead of the point.
The production imposes the director's signature wink-wink style on the material to a suffocating degree.
Theatre Company's exceptionally charming revival of The Robber Bridegroom is exactly the kind of intimate extravaganza you would expect

The Robber Bridegroom is a worthy choice; the show, done well, is offbeat but a thorough charmer.
